description: Multi-token meaning units (longest match against JMdict). Shared rule data: the Python analyzer reads it today and a browser engine can read the same file. Variants map colloquial spellings to the standard forms JMdict lists; they are tried only when the written form has no entry. Units whose best entry's first sense has a part of speech listed in clause_initial_only_pos (e.g. しまった 'oh no') are accepted only at the start of a clause, so 食べてしまった is not read as an interjection. Conjunctions are not restricted, because clause-linking ones (のに, けど) belong mid-sentence; a single-entry でも mid-sentence still shows 'but' first (known limitation). When a span begins or ends with a particle or auxiliary token, only entries whose first sense is functional (function_edge_entry_pos), or common entries with a function_edge_common_pos, count; は+と is not 'pigeon' and し+て is not 'doer'. Part-of-speech names match JMdict labels by prefix ("particle" does not match "nouns which may take the genitive case particle"). A span containing a verb or adjective token is never read as a bare particle (verb し + て is not the particle して). Units never start on a token in never_initial_surfaces: the past ending た, the connective て and the object marker を only close or link words (た+し is not 'want to', を+して is not the causative particle). Mid-clause, entries whose first sense is in clause_initial_preferred_pos rank after the others (でも in 僕でも is 'even', not 'but').
